scientific_question: Given one completed strong-Agent session and its exact ready-to-submit program C0, does one official-path target-state execution result cause a matched continuation T to produce more final EnvBench Official passes than an equal continuation C1 receiving no execution result?
scope: Consumed Dev mechanism falsification only. No protected Canary or Official Test access, representative effect estimate, SOTA claim, or leaderboard claim.
retained_mechanism: One strong Agent active-session lineage plus complete-program target-state replay feedback. No structured state, checkpoint graph, frontier, cross-case memory, package rule, or bootstrap minimization.

eligible_population_definition.source: All previously consumed Dev projects found in completed gpt-5.6-sol xhigh strong-Agent studies as of preregistration that formed an admissible complete program and received a valid postepisode EnvBench Official nonpass for a deployment reason.
excluded: pure source-acquisition, package-delivery, evaluator-install, or transport censoring
duplicate sessions for the same project
cases selected using a prior treatment outcome

cases.prior_nonpass: bootstrap failed because pkg_resources was unavailable

paired_design.C0: The exact complete program already emitted by the historical completed strong-Agent session; no new model call.
paired_design.C1: One tool-free native Codex fork from the completed C0 session receiving the typed-null replay schema and one revision opportunity.
paired_design.T: One tool-free native Codex fork from the identical completed C0 session receiving one real official-path target-state replay payload and one revision opportunity.
paired_design.unique_causal_difference: Real target-state replay field values versus typed-null field values. Model, reasoning effort, completed prefix, output schema, tools, revision count, and postepisode executor are matched.
paired_design.continuation_tools: none for both C1 and T

executor.online: EnvBenchCandidateExecutor on Spark through RemoteEnvBenchProcessRunner; result disclosed only to T.
executor.postepisode: C0, C1, and T each execute independently through the same EnvBench candidate-execution classes on Spark; no result returns to any Agent.
executor.known_fidelity_counterexample: The old nested replay passed mflowgen while Official failed due bind-mount Git ownership. The replacement executor reproduced exit_code=1 and git_ownership_error=true on the same historical program before this preregistration.

censoring.online_execution: Retry exact C0 bytes only after recognized source-acquisition, package-delivery, evaluator-install, or transport failure. Do not branch on a censored payload. After three unresolved attempts, retain the case as censored without replacement.
censoring.postepisode_execution: Apply the same exact-program retry policy independently to each arm. Never regenerate a program after postepisode evidence.
censoring.semantic_nonpass: Any completed candidate execution with bootstrap failure or nonzero issues remains a valid nonpass and is not retried as infrastructure.

analysis.primary_contrast: T-exclusive Official wins versus C1-exclusive Official wins
analysis.supporting_causal_chain: The real replay exposes a concrete counterexample, T changes the program in a corresponding way, T Official-passes, and C1 does not.
secondary: C0, C1, and T Official Pass@1
continuation input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens
online replay and postepisode wall time

decision_rule.retain_for_next_cross-progress_experimen: At least two independent supporting causal chains, more T-exclusive than C1-exclusive Official wins, and no executor-fidelity contradiction.
decision_rule.retain_weak: Exactly one supporting causal chain with no C1-exclusive win; do not promote or enter protected evaluation.
decision_rule.kill_current_replay_core: No supporting causal chain, or T-exclusive wins do not exceed C1-exclusive wins after all valid pairs complete.
decision_rule.insufficient: Fewer than four valid paired projects after predeclared censoring; do not replace cases or claim an effect.

safeguard_note: This is a scientific preregistration, not a new runtime gate or frozen software contract. Git records it; ordinary tests check branch and executor parity.
